Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 83, verses 1–4:

Naming of the surah

• It is called al-Mutaffifin (Those Who Give Short Measure), because it opens with a warning of punishment for the mutaffifin, those who give short measure and weight and who withhold people's rights.

Some of the surah's objectives

• To warn people against short-changing in measure and weight, and to admonish them that they will be held to account for this on the Day of Resurrection, when they stand before their Lord.

• To speak of the wretched who deny the Day of Recompense and the Qur'an, to depict their recompense on the Day of Resurrection, and to contrast them with the mention of the state of the God-fearing righteous, and of some of their bliss; and to describe the condition of the two groups in this transient world, by mentioning the harm the deniers inflicted and their mockery of the believers, and the final outcome of both groups on the Day of Resurrection.

[The Tafsir]

﴿Woe to those who give short measure,﴾ those who, when they take a measure or weight from people, take their full due for themselves, but when they measure or weigh out to others, they give less. So how much more so is the case of one who steals and embezzles them and withholds people's possessions? Such a person is more deserving of the warning than those who give short measure and weight. Do those who give short measure not believe that Allah will resurrect them and call them to account for their deeds?

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 83, verses 7–9:

Indeed, the destiny of the wicked and their abode is truly in confinement. And what will make you know what this confinement is? It is an enduring prison and a painful punishment. It is the destination that was decreed for them, a matter written and settled, neither increased nor decreased.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 83, verses 7–9:

Indeed, the destiny of the wicked and their abode is truly in confinement. And what will make you know what this confinement is? It is an enduring prison and a painful punishment. It is the destination that was decreed for them, a matter written and settled, neither increased nor decreased.

Severe punishment on that Day for those who deny, who deny the occurrence of the Day of Recompense. None deny it except every sinful transgressor, who, when Our verses are recited to him, says: "These are the fables of the ancients." The matter is not as they claim; rather, it is the speech of Allah and His revelation to His Prophet. What has veiled their hearts from believing in it is what has covered them of the great amount of sins they commit. The matter is not as the disbelievers claim; rather, on the Day of Resurrection they will indeed be veiled from seeing their Lord—Exalted is He and High. In this verse is an indication of the believers seeing their Lord in Paradise. Then they will surely enter the Fire and suffer its heat. Then it will be said to them: "This is the reward that you used to deny."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 83, verses 18–21:

Truly, the record of the righteous (al-abrar), who are the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), is indeed in the lofty ranks in Paradise. And what will make you know, O Messenger, what these lofty ranks are? The record of the righteous is a written book, settled and decided, neither increased nor decreased in it, and the angels nearest to God from every heaven look upon it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 83, verse 22–28:

Indeed, the righteous and the obedient will be in Paradise, enjoying delights. On couches they will gaze upon their Lord, and upon what He has prepared for them of good things. You will see in their faces the radiance of bliss. They will be given to drink of pure wine, its seal sealed with musk, the last of it a scent of musk. And for that lasting bliss let those who compete, compete. This drink is mixed with a spring in Paradise known as "Tasnim," for its loftiness, a spring prepared so that the nearest (to Allah) may drink from it and be delighted by it.

Indeed, those who committed crime used to mock the believers in the worldly life. And when they passed by them, they would wink at one another in derision, mocking them. And when those who committed crime returned to their own people and families, they would amuse themselves with mockery of the believers. And when these disbelievers saw the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), who had followed guidance, they said: "Indeed, these are misguided in their following of Muhammad (ﷺ)." But these criminals were not sent as watchers over the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ).

On the couches of honour, the believers gaze upon what Allah has bestowed on them of dignity and delight in Paradise, and among the greatest of that is gazing upon the Noble Face of Allah. "Have the disbelievers been recompensed in kind for what they used to do?" Yes, they will be recompensed in full, and with the most just recompense, fitting what they used to do in the world of evil deeds and sins.
